findings-against-prior-runs.prior-run: this run, items decision-record-and-replay through decision-semantica-import (morning of 2026-11-11)
findings-against-prior-runs.prior-claim: The decision MCP tools work: pass.
findings-against-prior-runs.what-is-actually-true: The server-side behaviour passes. Claude Code, however, rejects every decision tool reply, because structuredContent fails the advertised outputSchema.
findings-against-prior-runs.evidence: Owner report for 2.5.1 (record/get/query/precedents/register fail in Claude Code; preview and the CLI work). Reproduced on 2.6.0 by schema_check.py: 6 of 6 successful calls invalid.
findings-against-prior-runs.so-what: The driver mcp.py read only content[0].text, so no decision item could fail on the client contract. The new decision-tool-replies-match-output-schema item checks it directly. Agents must use the decisions CLI until the server is fixed (ai-badger #667 documents the fallback).

items.expected-result: every tool in derived.mcp-tool-count and every prompt in derived.mcp-prompt-count is listed and reachable

items.observed-result: tools/list returns 43 tools, which matches the derived mcp-tool-count. The tools were listed, not all called; prompts were not exercised in this pass.

items.expected-result: Validate every decision tool's structuredContent against the outputSchema that tools/list advertises (jsonschema Draft 2020-12), the way Claude Code does, for record_decision, get_decision, query_decisions, find_decision_precedents, get_decision_graph and preview_decisions. Every reply must validate. A raw JSON-RPC client that reads only content[0].text cannot fail this item, so the other decision items do not cover it. (ADR-0142; MCP structured output)
items.evidence: record_decision: INVALID at data/value: 'changeReason' is a required property; get_decision: INVALID at data/value/versions/0: 'changeReason' is a required property; query_decisions: INVALID at data/value: 'nextAfterId' is a required property; find_decision_precedents: INVALID at data/value: 'nextAfterId' ...; get_decision_graph: INVALID at meta: 'promotionsWaitTimeSeconds' is a required property; preview_decisions: INVALID at meta: 'promotionsWaitTimeSeconds' ...; invalid tools: 6. 13 of 43 tools advertise an outputSchema, all of them decision tools.
items.observed-result: Every successful decision call returns structuredContent that fails its own outputSchema. Null-valued properties are left out of the reply, but the schema lists them as required. Claude Code rejects the reply after the server has already committed the write. In practice preview_decisions works in Claude Code (owner report), even though it fails strict validation on meta.

items.expected-result: On a chain X1 depends_on X2 depends_on X3, get_decision_graph from X1 upstream: depth 0 = seed alone with truncated reason depth; depth 1 = 2 nodes, reason depth; depth 2 = 3 nodes, not truncated; maxNodes 2 = 2 nodes, reason nodes. downstream from X1 returns the seed alone (direction control). depth 11 and maxNodes 0 -> invalid-argument. Upstream = edges whose source is the node (DecisionService.Views.cs). (ADR-0142, docs/how-to/record-project-decisions.md)
items.evidence: upstream depth 0 -> nodes 1, truncated, reasons [depth]; depth 1 -> nodes 2 edges 1, [depth]; depth 2 -> nodes 3 edges 2, not truncated; depth 2 maxNodes 2 -> nodes 2, [nodes]; downstream depth 2 -> nodes 1; depth 11 -> invalid-argument: ... must be in the range given by <0> and <11>, was <11>; maxNodes 0 -> invalid-argument ... <1> and <501>, was <0>
items.observed-result: Depth and node limits truncate and report the reason; out-of-range values are refused. The refusal text shows an exclusive upper bound ('<0> and <11>, was <11>'), which reads as if 11 were allowed: a wording defect, not a behaviour one. The first driver attempt used downstream and saw the seed alone; that was a driver error about direction, not a product defect.
